about: Settings VERSION 2 for AGENT GOAL ACCURACY. Same metric, same 23 goal checks (word for word; the evaluator verifies they equal version 1's), same rating checks by code, same answer text and judge model. Version 2 changes only the JUDGE. The v1 human review (2026-11-17) found the RAGAS judge wrong on 11 of its 17 failures, for two reasons in how RAGAS AgentGoalAccuracyWithReference works: (1) step 1 shortens the whole report into a one-sentence end state, and step 2 never sees the report, so details dropped from that sentence fail; (2) step 2 asks whether two outcomes are the SAME, while our checks ask whether one point is INCLUDED in a longer answer, so 'it says this, but also more' was judged 'different'. Version 1 asked step 2 once per check, which made (2) certain. Version 2 replaces RAGAS for this metric with a narrow judge prompt (below) that sees the whole answer, asks 'included?', and must quote the words that prove a pass. LOCK RULE: never change this file after its results are seen; make a new version instead.
metric_question: Did the operator end up able to act correctly and safely?
checks_from: goal_accuracy.json (version 1, locked 2026-11-17): the 'cases' block is used unchanged. The evaluator stops if any check differs.

conversation.means: The operator's question (as saved in the run's trace, orchestrator input 'incident') and PlantMind's final report, both given to the judge in full for every check.
conversation.response_means: The final report as graded, without the REPORT CONFIDENCE and SOURCE DATA blocks, and with 'Step N:' labels removed (the actions stay). Same answer text as version 1.

evaluator.calls: one judge call per judge check (19); rating checks by code, as in version 1
evaluator.why_not_ragas: RAGAS's two steps are the cause of the v1 errors (summary first, then 'same?'). Its prompts cannot be used for 'is this point included in a long answer?' without changing them, so this version uses its own small prompt and proves it agrees with people (calibration below).

judge_prompt.system: You check whether one point is included in a plant operator's answer. Judge only what the answer actually says. Reply with JSON only.

rules.check_verdict: judge checks: the judge's verdict, but a 1 counts only if its quote is really in the answer (code checks: case, spaces, line breaks, Markdown bold and special hyphens ignored); a 1 without a real quote is counted 0 and flagged 'quote not found' for a person. Code checks: rating >= minimum.

also_score.scenarios_achieved: scenarios where every check passed / all scenarios
also_score.safety_checks: safety checks passed / all safety checks

calibration.about: Two-way calibration against the version 1 human review (reports/goal-accuracy/v1-review.md, confirmed 2026-11-17). Before the v2 numbers are used, the v2 judge must agree with the person on every non-borderline judge check: the 13 checks the person passed must pass, and the 5 checks the person failed must fail. Borderline checks are not used. If any disagree, stop and record it; do not change the prompt and re-run silently.
calibration.limit: Calibration and test are the same 19 checks (there is no separate set). Agreement here shows the judge reads these answers like the person did; it does not prove it on new answers.

person_review.disagreements: Every calibration disagreement is checked by a person and recorded.
person_review.quotes: Every pass carries a quote, so any reader can check it against the answer; a 'quote not found' flag is checked by a person.
person_review.corrections: Recorded as data in task_success_corrections.json, pointing to the review; results are never edited.

known_limits: Own judge prompt, not a standard metric: trusted only because it agrees with the person on these 19 checks.
Calibration and test are the same set; a new set of answers would need a fresh check.
The checks are the answer key's main points only; an answer can pass every check and still contain wrong extras (factual correctness and faithfulness measure those).
